questions.learningObjective: Distinguish outbound NAT from inbound access
questions.stem: What network capability does CLZ-280's NAT Gateway association provide to a future workload in web-snet?

options.A: An unsolicited inbound RDP endpoint on every private NIC
options.B: HTTP path-based load balancing across two Windows VMs
options.C: Explicit outbound Internet connectivity using the configured public IP
options.D: Automatic guest authentication through Microsoft Entra ID

optionExplanations.A: NAT Gateway does not publish inbound port forwarding.
optionExplanations.B: That is not the purpose of NAT Gateway.
optionExplanations.C: NAT Gateway supplies source translation for connections initiated from the associated subnet.
optionExplanations.D: The service handles networking rather than guest identity.

questions.stem: Which Terraform output is intended for an external system's egress-IP allowlist?

options.A: nat_gateway_public_ip
options.B: resource_group_name
options.C: location
options.D: The web subnet's private address prefix

optionExplanations.A: It exposes the Standard public IP associated with the NAT Gateway.
optionExplanations.B: A logical container name is not the translated source IP.
optionExplanations.C: The region name does not identify the egress endpoint.
optionExplanations.D: External Internet services see the translated public source, not the private subnet range.

questions.stem: Which subnet is associated with NAT Gateway in the current CLZ-280 configuration?

options.A: Every subnet in every VNet in the subscription
options.B: web-snet only
options.C: AzureBastionSubnet only
options.D: The local contributor's Wi-Fi network

optionExplanations.A: Association is explicit and limited.
optionExplanations.B: The code declares azurerm_subnet_nat_gateway_association.web.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson does not create that Bastion subnet.
optionExplanations.D: Azure subnet association does not attach the workstation LAN.

questions.stem: Why does CLZ-280 report control-plane configuration rather than claiming a successful workload egress test?

options.A: A NAT Gateway can never support real outbound traffic
options.B: Terraform state already contains a captured Internet packet trace
options.C: The lesson creates no workload to originate a data-plane connection
options.D: The public IP output secretly runs a Windows browser

optionExplanations.A: Supporting outbound traffic is its purpose.
optionExplanations.B: State does not provide that network test.
optionExplanations.C: Resource existence and subnet association are verifiable, but runtime egress needs a client.
optionExplanations.D: Printing an IP does not create a guest workload.

questions.stem: Which relationships complete the lesson's explicit NAT design?

options.A: Only a Role tag on the public IP
options.B: A public-IP association and a web-subnet association to the NAT Gateway
options.C: Only a Windows administrator password output
options.D: Only a health probe attached to a private DNS zone

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not establish either relationship.
optionExplanations.B: The gateway needs both its public source identity and the subnet scope.
optionExplanations.C: No guest credential is needed by this control-plane-only topology.
optionExplanations.D: Neither object provides the declared NAT associations.

questions.stem: A future VM in app-snet uses another egress path while web-snet has NAT Gateway. What is the first scope check?

options.A: Whether the VM's computer name includes web
options.B: Whether the current public IP output has enough characters
options.C: Whether the book has been downloaded
options.D: Whether the VM's NIC is actually in a subnet associated with the NAT Gateway

optionExplanations.A: Names do not determine subnet NAT association.
optionExplanations.B: String length does not define scope.
optionExplanations.C: Book access has no effect on Azure routing.
optionExplanations.D: The configured web association does not cover app-snet.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why inbound administration stays absent
questions.stem: A learner tries to open RDP to nat_gateway_public_ip from the Internet. Why is this not the lesson's administration path?

options.A: NAT Gateway does not accept unsolicited inbound connections to private workloads
options.B: The gateway requires the Windows password in its DNS label
options.C: All public IPv4 addresses support RDP automatically
options.D: Changing the client port to 80 creates RDP forwarding

optionExplanations.A: Use an approved management path such as Bastion or VPN instead.
optionExplanations.B: The service does not authenticate guests that way.
optionExplanations.C: An address alone does not publish a listener.
optionExplanations.D: No inbound rule is created by a different client port.

questions.stem: How can an Internet service return data for a connection initiated by a private VM through NAT Gateway?

options.A: The service tracks the outbound flow and permits matching response traffic
options.B: The service temporarily opens all inbound ports to everyone
options.C: The administrator creates an inbound NAT rule for every download packet
options.D: The private VM must attach a second public IP after sending each request

optionExplanations.A: Return packets are associated with the initiated flow.
optionExplanations.B: Matching return traffic does not imply universal inbound exposure.
optionExplanations.C: Established-flow responses do not need per-download inbound rules.
optionExplanations.D: That is not required for subnet NAT egress.

questions.stem: An organization needs to block outbound connections to unapproved destinations. What is the limitation of this NAT-only lesson?

options.A: NAT Gateway automatically blocks every destination not listed in Terraform tags
options.B: The public IP encrypts destination names and makes policy unnecessary
options.C: Changing the source IP always proves the destination is safe
options.D: NAT Gateway provides egress translation rather than a destination-inspection firewall

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not create a destination allowlist.
optionExplanations.B: An egress IP is not a substitute for policy.
optionExplanations.C: Source translation does not assess destination trust.
optionExplanations.D: Use appropriate filtering and inspection controls in the production design.

questions.stem: A VM in the associated web subnet has an outbound NSG deny for its target service. Does NAT Gateway bypass that deny?

options.A: Yes; every associated subnet becomes exempt from NSGs
options.B: No; source translation does not override the effective security policy
options.C: Yes; a Standard public IP always permits all protocols
options.D: No; because NAT Gateway never supports TCP

optionExplanations.A: Association does not remove NSG enforcement.
optionExplanations.B: The traffic still needs an allowed network path.
optionExplanations.C: Public addressing is not an unconditional policy allow.
optionExplanations.D: TCP outbound connectivity is supported.

questions.stem: A production subnet has a 0.0.0.0/0 user-defined route to a virtual appliance. What should be checked when observed egress differs from the NAT IP?

options.A: Only whether the NAT public IP is printed in the README
options.B: Only whether the Project tag uses title case
options.C: The effective route and the appliance's outbound design
options.D: Only whether the Terraform output is marked sensitive

optionExplanations.A: Documentation text does not control effective routing.
optionExplanations.B: Tag casing is unrelated to the chosen next hop.
optionExplanations.C: A custom default route to an appliance can override the direct Internet path.
optionExplanations.D: Output redaction does not determine routing.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish DNS resolution from egress identity
questions.stem: An Internet name fails to resolve inside a future VM. Does the NAT IP alone prove DNS is configured correctly?

options.A: Yes; NAT Gateway automatically hosts every public DNS zone
options.B: No; resolver configuration and name-resolution tests are separate
options.C: Yes; a Standard public IP creates an A record for every name
options.D: No; because DNS can only run from public VMs

optionExplanations.A: It does not provide that DNS hosting function.
optionExplanations.B: Source NAT is not an authoritative DNS or resolver service.
optionExplanations.C: An IP resource does not create arbitrary DNS records.
optionExplanations.D: Private clients can use DNS with an appropriate resolver path.

questions.stem: Which IP resource matches CLZ-280's declared Standard NAT Gateway design?

options.A: A Standard static public IPv4 in the intended region
options.B: A Basic dynamic public IP from another region
options.C: A private /24 subnet prefix without a public IP
options.D: A Windows administrator username formatted as an IP label

optionExplanations.A: The lesson declares Standard SKU and Static allocation.
optionExplanations.B: That does not match the supported Standard association.
optionExplanations.C: The declared translation design needs a public source identity.
optionExplanations.D: A username is not a compatible public IP resource.

questions.stem: Which Azure CLI observation most directly confirms the web subnet association?

options.A: The Windows VM's power state is running
options.B: The resource group has four tags
options.C: web-snet's natGateway.id references the expected NAT resource
options.D: The local terraform directory contains a README

optionExplanations.A: This lesson creates no VM, and VM power does not identify subnet association.
optionExplanations.B: Tags are not the NAT relationship.
optionExplanations.C: That field describes the subnet's configured gateway relationship.
optionExplanations.D: Local documentation does not prove Azure association.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish provisioned state from workload testing
questions.stem: NAT Gateway is Succeeded and references the expected public IP. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Every possible destination has been tested successfully
options.B: The gateway has installed IIS on an unseen VM
options.C: The private DNS record web.clz.internal is now guaranteed to resolve
options.D: The configured control-plane resources are present; a workload test would provide additional egress evidence

optionExplanations.A: No workload test has exercised destinations.
optionExplanations.B: No VM or IIS deployment exists in this lesson.
optionExplanations.C: Private DNS is taught separately.
optionExplanations.D: Provisioning success is narrower than an observed data-plane connection.

questions.stem: Why can CLZ-280 incur charges even though it creates no VM and sends no workload traffic?

options.A: NAT Gateway has a provisioned-service hourly charge and its public IP is billable
options.B: Terraform charges for every plan command sent to Azure
options.C: The VNet's private address count is the hourly charge
options.D: Each README view launches an Azure VM

optionExplanations.A: Idle configuration is not necessarily free.
optionExplanations.B: Planning is not the declared billable NAT service.
optionExplanations.C: Private address-space size is not this service's main cost driver.
optionExplanations.D: The static learning site does not create compute.

questions.stem: Which traffic change can increase NAT Gateway's usage-based cost in addition to its provisioned hourly cost?

options.A: Changing the Terraform resource label from main to web
options.B: More processed outbound and return data
options.C: Choosing the browser's light theme
options.D: Adding a paragraph to the lesson README

optionExplanations.A: Local labels do not meter network data.
optionExplanations.B: Data-processing charges vary with traffic volume.
optionExplanations.C: Site appearance does not add Azure NAT processing.
optionExplanations.D: Documentation size is not workload traffic through this NAT Gateway.

questions.stem: The exercise associates app-snet with the existing NAT Gateway. What new Terraform relationship is required?

options.A: An inbound RDP rule for every app subnet address
options.B: A second administrator password generated by the gateway
options.C: A subnet-to-NAT-Gateway association for app-snet
options.D: A load-balancer health probe on port 53

optionExplanations.A: Inbound administration is not required for outbound subnet association.
optionExplanations.B: The gateway does not need a Windows guest credential.
optionExplanations.C: One gateway can serve multiple appropriate subnets in the same VNet.
optionExplanations.D: A health probe is not a NAT association.

questions.stem: Can one subnet be directly associated with two NAT Gateway resources simultaneously?

options.A: No; a subnet can have one NAT Gateway association
options.B: Yes; every new outbound flow alternates between all gateways
options.C: Yes; but only when both public IPs are dynamic
options.D: No; because NAT Gateway can serve only one VM

optionExplanations.A: Choose the intended gateway for that subnet.
optionExplanations.B: The association does not provide that multi-gateway pool.
optionExplanations.C: That is not a supported basis for multiple gateway association.
optionExplanations.D: It can serve many private workloads in associated subnets.

questions.stem: Can the same Standard NAT Gateway be directly associated with subnets in two different VNets?

options.A: Yes; every subnet sharing the same name is automatically covered
options.B: Yes; a common Project tag makes all VNets one network
options.C: No; because NAT Gateway cannot associate with any subnet
options.D: No; its subnet associations must be within one VNet

optionExplanations.A: Subnet names do not join scope across VNets.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not merge network boundaries.
optionExplanations.C: Subnet association is its core configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Cross-VNet egress requires an appropriate routing architecture rather than direct spanning.

questions.stem: Why is NAT Gateway's dynamic SNAT-port allocation different from CLZ-270 autoscaling?

options.A: It creates a new VM for every allocated SNAT port
options.B: It scales outbound connection translation capacity rather than the number of Windows VMs
options.C: It changes autoscale CPU thresholds automatically
options.D: It replaces the VMSS operating system with a network appliance

optionExplanations.A: Translation ports do not represent VM instances.
optionExplanations.B: The service manages network flows, not this lesson's compute fleet.
optionExplanations.C: Those rules target the VMSS independently.
optionExplanations.D: The service does not transform guest compute.

questions.stem: A workload will open many simultaneous outbound connections. What belongs in the NAT design review?

options.A: Connection demand, SNAT capacity, destinations, and public IP or prefix sizing
options.B: Only the number of letters in the resource-group name
options.C: Only the desired IIS page title
options.D: Only the VM administrator's surname

optionExplanations.A: Network connection scale can require a deliberate capacity design.
optionExplanations.B: Name length does not describe connection demand.
optionExplanations.C: Page text is not a translation-capacity measure.
optionExplanations.D: Guest naming does not determine SNAT capacity.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish source identity from content confidentiality
questions.stem: Does a stable NAT public IP encrypt all application traffic automatically?

options.A: Yes; a static address always implies HTTPS
options.B: Yes; Terraform tags act as network encryption keys
options.C: No; applications still need suitable transport encryption such as TLS
options.D: No; because private workloads cannot use HTTPS

optionExplanations.A: An IP allocation method does not enable TLS.
optionExplanations.B: Tags are metadata.
optionExplanations.C: Source translation changes addressing, not application encryption.
optionExplanations.D: Private clients can initiate TLS connections through appropriate egress.

questions.learningObjective: Explain explicit egress for private Windows workloads
questions.stem: Why would a later private Windows workload need a declared egress path for updates or activation?

options.A: Bastion automatically supplies all Internet downloads for guest processes
options.B: Private Internet-bound services require an allowed explicit outbound method
options.C: Private VMs never need network communication
options.D: The lesson's resource-group tags reserve update bandwidth

optionExplanations.A: Management connectivity is not a general guest egress promise.
optionExplanations.B: NAT Gateway is one option for that path.
optionExplanations.C: Private workloads can need updates, activation, and dependencies.
optionExplanations.D: Tags do not establish connectivity.

questions.stem: Does completing CLZ-280 automatically attach its NAT Gateway to the VMSS deployed in CLZ-270's separate VNet?

options.A: Yes; sequential lesson numbers automatically connect Azure resources
options.B: Yes; all resources with the same environment tag share a subnet
options.C: No; because NAT Gateway cannot work with VMSS
options.D: No; the lesson declares its own VNet and subnet association

optionExplanations.A: Navigation order does not create networking relationships.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not attach NICs to networks.
optionExplanations.C: It can serve scale-set instances in appropriately associated subnets.
optionExplanations.D: Previous deployments are not implicitly modified by this new configuration.

questions.stem: An external partner allowlists the NAT public IP. What must be considered if the lab is destroyed and recreated?

options.A: The partner's policy automatically follows the Terraform variable name
options.B: The public address may change, so the partner's allowlist must be reviewed
options.C: The resource-group tag permanently reserves the IP forever
options.D: The gateway retains every previous public IP after destroy

optionExplanations.A: External systems do not watch local Terraform names.
optionExplanations.B: Destroying and recreating IP resources does not guarantee the same allocated address.
optionExplanations.C: Tags do not reserve deleted public IPs.
optionExplanations.D: Destroyed resources are not retained by that assumption.

questions.stem: A subnet has both NAT Gateway and a load-balancer outbound rule without an overriding appliance route. Which method normally handles new outbound flows?

options.A: The load-balancer inbound HTTP rule always wins
options.B: The Terraform output printed most recently
options.C: Whichever guest has the shorter computer name
options.D: The associated NAT Gateway

optionExplanations.A: Inbound HTTP forwarding is not the priority rule for new egress flows.
optionExplanations.B: Printing order does not control Azure routing.
optionExplanations.C: Guest naming does not choose the egress mechanism.
optionExplanations.D: NAT Gateway takes precedence over the other explicit Internet egress method for new flows.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish shared egress identity from workload attribution
questions.stem: A partner sees the same NAT public IP for requests from two private clients. Can that source IP alone identify which VM initiated each request?

options.A: Yes; NAT Gateway gives every private client a different public IP automatically
options.B: Yes; the public IP embeds the VM's Terraform resource address
options.C: No; shared egress requires application identity and appropriate logs for attribution
options.D: No; NAT Gateway removes every application authentication header

optionExplanations.A: Multiple clients can share the configured NAT public address.
optionExplanations.B: A translated address does not embed a Terraform identity.
optionExplanations.C: The shared source identifies an egress path, not a unique guest or application principal.
optionExplanations.D: Source translation does not remove application authentication; use it alongside operational logs.

questions.stem: A learner removes only the subnet association and leaves NAT Gateway and its public IP provisioned. What cost concern remains?

options.A: The provisioned gateway and public IP can still incur charges
options.B: No charges are possible without an associated VM
options.C: Only the local Terraform state file becomes billable
options.D: The VNet automatically deletes the unattached gateway

optionExplanations.A: Removing scope is not the same as deleting billable resources.
optionExplanations.B: Idle gateways can still be billable.
optionExplanations.C: The charges belong to Azure services.
optionExplanations.D: Do not assume automatic deletion of separate resources.

questions.stem: Which final evidence is appropriate after CLZ-280's documented terraform destroy?

options.A: A failed RDP connection to the NAT public IP alone
options.B: A private DNS lookup returns NXDOMAIN
options.C: The browser gallery shows a NAT icon
options.D: az group exists returns false for the captured lesson group

optionExplanations.A: The gateway never promised inbound RDP, so that is not cleanup evidence.
optionExplanations.B: Private DNS is unrelated to this lesson's NAT cleanup.
optionExplanations.C: A visual explains topology but does not show live resource absence.
optionExplanations.D: The check confirms the managed gateway, IP, and group footprint is gone.
